docs.title: PRD — AAuth sandbox
docs.text: Initiative: INIT-AAUTHGO-002 Repository: github.com/aauth-dev/aauth-go

docs.title: Problem
docs.text:
AAuth has four server roles: agent provider, resource, person server (PS) and access server (AS). Trying a flow end to end, testing an implementation of one role, or running a workshop needs all of them running together with real keys, real tokens and real HTTP message signatures. aauth-go implements every role, and its end-to-end tests and walkthrough examples already wire them up in-process, but nothing packages them as servers that a developer, an HTTP client such as Postman, or another implementation can talk to.

Two things make this harder than starting four HTTP servers:

  • Server identifiers are https:// origins with a domain name and no port (draft-11 §11.1). A laptop setup needs TLS, distinct hostnames per role, and port 443.
  • Every request is signed (RFC 9421) with an Ed25519 or ES256 key, presenting a token in Signature-Key. General-purpose HTTP clients cannot do this themselves.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
• One command starts every role on a laptop, with trusted TLS, hostnames per role, and all five access modes available.
  • Any role can be replaced by an external implementation, so the sandbox can test someone's PS, AS, resource or agent provider.
  • HTTP clients that cannot sign (Postman, curl, Newman) can still drive the agent side of every flow.
  • The same binary runs as one container per role in Docker Compose, and as separate deployments on minikube.
  • Every message the sandbox's roles send and receive is recorded, so tools can show the server-to-server steps a client never sees.

docs.title: Non-Goals
docs.text:
• Production deployment, high availability, or durable storage beyond local files.
  • A user interface beyond minimal consent and interaction pages.
  • An HTTP (non-TLS) mode for the protocol. The sandbox runs AAuth as specified; there is no bypass in the SDK.

docs.title: Topology and identity
docs.text:
1. Roles. A sandbox configuration lists roles: an agent provider, a PS, an AS, and resources. Each role is local (served by the sandbox) or remote (an external URL). Two demo resources cover the access modes: one whose resource tokens name the PS (agent identity, resource-managed, person identity, PS authorization) and one with its own AS (federated authorization).
  2. Names. Default hostnames use the reserved .test domain: ap.aauth.test, resource.aauth.test, docs.aauth.test, ps.aauth.test, as.aauth.test. aauth-sandbox hosts prints the /etc/hosts lines for a laptop.
  3. TLS. On first run the sandbox creates a development certificate authority in its state directory and issues certificates for the configured names. aauth-sandbox ca export writes the CA certificate for Postman, browsers or the system trust store.
  4. One listener. Locally, all roles share one TLS listener on port 443 and are routed by host name, because identifiers cannot carry ports.
  5. Keys. Each role's signing key is generated on first run and persisted. --fixed-keys uses the published test keys from the walkthrough (RFC 8037's Ed25519 example key and the walkthrough's generated keys), so messages carry the same thumbprints the PIDL viewer shows. Fixed keys are refused for names outside .test.

docs.title: Flows
docs.text:
1. Demo resources serve a small documents API with the endpoints the walkthrough uses: signed access for agent identity, interaction and an AAuth-Access session for resource-managed access, person-token access, an authorization endpoint, and auth-token access.
  2. Consent. The PS and the resource-managed resource serve minimal consent and interaction pages. consent: auto approves immediately; consent: manual waits for a person in a browser. In sandbox mode a headless approval endpoint lets automated runs approve a pending interaction by code.
  3. Agent. The sandbox holds a test agent: it enrolls with the agent provider and keeps a current agent token, for use by the signing helper.

docs.title: Clients that cannot sign
docs.text:
1. Signing helper. aauth-sandbox sign listens on loopback only. A client sends an unsigned request to http://127.0.0.1:<port>/<target URL>; the helper adds Content-Digest for bodies, presents a token in Signature-Key (the agent token by default, or the token the client passes in a sandbox-only header), signs with the agent's key, forwards the request over TLS, and returns the response unchanged. It also answers POST /sign with the headers to add, for clients that send requests themselves.
  2. Token presentation. The client chooses the presented token with X-Sandbox-Present: agent|person|auth and, for person and auth tokens, X-Sandbox-Token. The helper strips both before forwarding.

docs.title: Observability
docs.text: 1. Trace. Every message a local role sends or receives is recorded in the JSON trace format of the end-to-end tests (RMI-AAUTHGO-016): sender and receiver roles, method, URL, status, ordered headers and bodies, and pointers to per-run values. GET /sandbox/trace returns it; DELETE /sandbox/trace clears it; --trace-file writes it continuously.

docs.title: Packaging
docs.text:
1. CLI aauth-sandbox with serve, sign, ca init|export, keys, hosts and trace, built with Cobra, installable with go install.
  2. Docker. One small image runs any role (serve --role ps) or all of them. A Compose file runs one container per role on a shared network with the .test names as network aliases, a volume for the CA and keys, and health checks.
  3. Kubernetes. Kustomize manifests with a minikube overlay: a Deployment and Service per role, an Ingress with the five host names and TLS from the sandbox CA, and instructions for minikube tunnel and hosts entries.

docs.title: Safety
docs.text: 1. The sandbox is a development tool. It prints a banner saying so, refuses fixed keys outside .test, serves sandbox-only endpoints (headless approval, trace) only in sandbox mode, and binds the signing helper to loopback only.

docs.title: Success Criteria
docs.text:
• aauth-sandbox serve followed by the walkthrough's requests through the signing helper completes all five access modes, with the trace showing the PS-to-AS federation.
  • Replacing the PS with an external URL runs the same flows against that PS.
  • docker compose up and the minikube overlay run the same flows with each role in its own container.
  • A Postman collection generated by PIDL runs green against the sandbox in Newman.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text:
• Built from aauth-go's own servers, so the sandbox exercises the code the Go samples show.
  • TLS and real names, no HTTP shortcut.
  • The CLI lives in the root module. Cobra and YAML become requirements of the module, but module graph pruning keeps them out of builds that import only the library, and go install works from a normal release tag.

docs.title: Packages
docs.text:
sandbox/                 library: no CLI or YAML dependencies
  config.go              Config, RoleConfig (local | remote URL), defaults
  ca.go                  development CA, certificates per name
  keys.go                key generation, persistence, fixed walkthrough keys
  resources.go           demo resources for the five access modes
  consent.go             consent and interaction pages, headless approval
  trace.go               trace recorder (RoundTripper and handler middleware)
  signer.go              signing helper handler
  sandbox.go             New(Config) (*Sandbox, error); Handler(); Close()

deploy/docker/           Dockerfile, compose.yaml
deploy/k8s/              kustomize base and overlays/minikube

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
state: ~/.aauth-sandbox        # CA, keys, enrollment
listen: :443
consent: auto                  # auto | manual
fixedKeys: false
roles:
  ap:       {host: ap.aauth.test}
  ps:       {host: ps.aauth.test}
  as:       {host: as.aauth.test}
  resource: {host: resource.aauth.test}            # resource tokens name the PS
  docs:     {host: docs.aauth.test, as: as}        # resource tokens name the AS
  # any role can be remote:
  # ps: {remote: https://ps.example.com}

Keys are camelCase, matching the YAML and JSON conventions of the project's other configuration.

docs.title: Routing and TLS
docs.text:
• A single http.Server with a tls.Config.GetCertificate that issues or loads a certificate for the SNI name, and a host-routing handler mapping each name to its role's http.Handler.
  • Outgoing requests between local roles use an http.Client that trusts the sandbox CA and resolves configured names to the listener, so no hosts entries are needed for server-to-server traffic.
  • serve --role <name> serves one role (containers); other roles are reached by name over the network.

docs.title: Signing helper
docs.text:
• http://127.0.0.1:<port>/https://resource.aauth.test/api/documents forwards to the URL after the first slash.
  • Body requests get Content-Digest (sha-256) and content-digest/content-type coverage, as aauth-go signs today.
  • Signature-Key presents the agent token by default; X-Sandbox-Present and X-Sandbox-Token select another token. Both headers are removed before forwarding.
  • POST /sign with {method, url, headers, body} returns {headers} to add.
  • The listener binds to 127.0.0.1 and ::1 only.

docs.title: Trace
docs.text: A RoundTripper wrapper on outgoing clients and a middleware on role handlers record exchanges with role names resolved from hosts. The recorder is bounded (ring buffer, default 10,000 exchanges) and shares the TraceExchange types of the end-to-end trace (RMI-AAUTHGO-016).

docs.title: Docker
docs.text:
• Multi-stage build: golang builder, gcr.io/distroless/static runtime, non-root user, CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE for 443.
  • compose.yaml: one service per role from the same image, network aliases for the .test names, a shared volume for the CA (created by an init service running ca init), health checks on each role's metadata endpoint.

docs.title: Kubernetes
docs.text:
• deploy/k8s/base: Deployment and Service per role, ConfigMap for the sandbox configuration, Secret for the CA, Ingress with TLS for the five hosts.
  • overlays/minikube: ingress-nginx annotations, image pull policy for local images, and a README for minikube tunnel and hosts entries.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
• Unit tests for configuration, CA issuance, routing, the signing helper and the trace.
  • An end-to-end test runs sandbox.New in-process with an in-memory listener and drives the five access modes through the signing helper.
  • CI builds the image and runs the end-to-end flow against Compose; the minikube run is documented and optional in CI.

docs.title: Implementation Notes
docs.text:
Phases 1 and 2 as built, where they differ from or refine the design above:

  • Configuration is flags, not YAML, for now: --state, --domain, --remote role=https://origin, --listen, --signer, --no-signer, --consent and --person. sandbox.Config holds the same settings for library use; a YAML file can map onto it later without new dependencies in the library.
  • Paths follow the draft-11 examples: agent provider POST /agent-token (two-key refresh, jkt-jwt) and POST /enroll (hwk); PS POST /person, POST /token, /pending/{id}, /interaction; AS POST /token, /pending/{id}; resources GET /api/documents, GET /api/data, POST /authorize, /pending/{id}, /interaction; every role's JWKS at /jwks.json.
  • One demo resource serves every access mode it can: /api/documents accepts an agent, person or auth token; /api/data is resource-managed. The session token is accepted as Authorization: AAuth (draft-11 §6.3) or AAuth-Access.
  • Location headers are made absolute by the sandbox router, as the draft's examples show them, so clients can follow them without knowing which server answered.
  • The signing helper declares the agent's capabilities: AAuth-Capabilities: interaction to the resources, and a capabilities member in JSON object bodies sent to the PS when the body has none (draft-11 §7.1, §7.2), before computing the digest. X-Sandbox-Capabilities overrides or empties the list. Without this, the draft's /token example body would be answered user_unreachable.
  • Presentation modes are agent, person, auth, hwk, jkt-jwt and none. The helper's agent has a durable and a current key; agent tokens from /agent-token through the helper are bound to the current key, so a client can pass them back in X-Sandbox-Token.
  • Trace types (sandbox.Exchange, sandbox.Message) live in the sandbox package; the end-to-end JSON trace (RMI-AAUTHGO-016) can adopt them.
  • Fixed walkthrough keys are not implemented yet. Keys are generated on first run and persisted, which keeps thumbprints stable across restarts.
  • Automatic consent approves at the moment an interaction is created; a request that waits (Prefer: wait) may therefore answer 200 directly instead of 202, and clients handle both.
